protocol: Live tool calls. One headless `claude -p` parent (claude-sonnet-5) per wave; each wave spawns the eval-<arm> subagents in parallel with only the question string. Main run: waves of up to 3 subagents per arm, arms interleaved. Waves with a missing or rate-limited run were discarded WHOLE and re-run as same-batch pairs (one best + one rich). Metrics from the child transcripts (toolUseResult).
headline: benchmark-trap: best 20/20 haiku, 10/10 sonnet, 10/10 opus; rich 0/20, 0/10, 6/10. rich's own computed alert compares EP-1 with Paris Proof 70 kWh/m2 and the models repeat it — the defect the audit (docs/building-profile-findings.md §7) predicted.

Shipped reference data: heating-season-held-out best 19/20 haiku, 10/10 sonnet, 10/10 opus vs rich 0/20, 5/10, 10/10; weather-single-quarter best 16/20, 10/10, 10/10 vs rich 0/20, 7/10, 10/10. On sonnet and opus best needs 1 weather call instead of 4-8, 15-27% fewer tokens.

Delivered description lines: solar-yield-check best 10/10 vs rich 1/10 (rich's performance-ratio rule sits past the 2,048 cut); select-hides-the-evidence sonnet best 9/10 vs rich 0/10 (rich's alert truncates at '(+6 more)' and sonnet invents the rest).

A NEW DEFECT in best: weather-partial-normalization best 0/10 vs rich 10/10. The shipped reference moves with the query year (Q1 2023 -> 2013-2022, Q1 2024 -> 2014-2023), so haiku normalises each quarter to a different denominator and reports a 6.6% improvement instead of 3.6%. Shipped data must be comparable across calls.
Everything else holds: controls 10/10 on every model; building questions >= 18/20; best cheaper in 30 of 32 shared cells (median -5.9% tokens).

P1.detail: every best building cell >= 18/20 (haiku) or 10/10; heat-pump-triage 18/20 is at the threshold

P3.detail: absent-sizing-input best 20/20, 0 fabrications. rich also 20/20; inline 6/10 with 4 fabricated kW/kWh sizing figures

P4.detail: haiku 16/20 (predicted >= 17, falsified at <= 12); median 1 weather call on sonnet and opus confirmed. 10 of the 16 correct haiku answers then extrapolate to a full year (~10,600 m3, arithmetically 4,200 x 2.53) — scored on the lead figure per Q16's rule

P5.detail: sonnet best 9/10, rich 0/10 (all 10 rich lists partial, several with invented days 05-13, 05-14, 05-26)

P6.detail: verdicts with the Van Beuningen boundary flagged 18/20, but BOTH margins (2.73 and 0.88) stated in only 10/20 (falsifier: < 15/20). rich 20/20 on verdicts, 0.88 stated in 0/20; 8 of 20 rich answers call the 100 kWh/m2 heat-pump boundary a 'Paris Proof target'

P7.detail: metered-vs-model and invented-label 10/10 on haiku and sonnet

P8.detail: best within -4.8..+0.7% of inline on the three shared questions; below rich on 7 of 8 tier-A questions (heat-pump-triage +0.7%)

P9.detail: 0 results replaced by a file notice

forecast-normalization: best 2/10, rich 4/10. best haiku makes NO call in 8 of 10 runs and asks for the gas figure; the description head's 'never weather-correct against forecast days' is read, the forecast tail is never shown. rich answers that do call apply the annual factor to 30 days (100.72).
Strong models need little here: opus rich is 10/10 on both weather questions, but with 7-8 weather calls and 36% more tokens than best.

infrastructure_incidents.open_meteo_quota: best's first reference-period implementation fetched one 10-year span per request (~260 Open-Meteo weighted calls). Under eval load it exhausted Open-Meteo's hourly quota and every best weather call returned 429. Fixed mid-run (commits after a366caf): window-sized fetches, sequential (Open-Meteo also rejects 10 concurrent requests), cached per location + window. Returned values unchanged (1,231.3 / 2,188.4 verified live before and after). All affected waves were discarded whole and re-run on the fixed deploy.
infrastructure_incidents.mcp_connection_race: In some headless parents the eval-rich MCP server was not yet connected when the Agent calls were made; the harness refused to spawn a tool-less subagent. Mitigated by a ToolSearch pre-call; affected waves re-run whole.
infrastructure_incidents.server_rate_limit: rich's own 30 req/min limiter tripped on multi-call haiku heat-pump waves; re-run as pairs.

scoring: Deterministic rubric per question (scratch harness, registered amendments applied), then every run the rubric could not classify read by hand — 46 manual verdicts, each with a reason in the run row. A 25-run random sample of rubric verdicts agreed with a hand reading. Borderline class kept visible: benchmark-trap answers that state the 17% gap and then reject the comparison are CORRECT (best 9, rich-opus 6, inline 7).

log_audit.method: Firestore toolCalls read directly (get_tool_call_log pages at 500 with no offset), per wave time window vs harness calls
log_audit.explained: all 6 mismatches are render_table calls rejected by input validation before the handler (never logged); per wave the difference equals the errored render_table calls exactly

caveats: best is a COMPOSITE; no gap here is attributable to one layer.
Same author for metadata, questions, ground truth and scoring. The held-out question was written after the build, before any run.
best was changed during the run (upstream-cost fix); response content was unchanged and every affected wave was re-run on the new deploy.
Repaired cells mix main-run waves (3+3) and repair pairs (1+1); both are same-batch comparisons.
